issue.title: Bug: memory_utilization checker reports false alarm in some GCU tests

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

In the GCU tests, the memory checker runs always before the GCU config rollback(to the default config) in the teardown of fixture setup_env. There maybe additional running config at that time comparing to when the base memory usage was collected. And also the system may be still handling the configuration change and is not in a stable state.

For example in the test tests/generic_config_updater/test_monitor_config.py, the memory checker reported a 10.5% overall memory increment but actually after the teardown, the memory usage dropped to the original level.

**ERROR    tests.common.plugins.memory_utilization:__init__.py:122 Memory errors detected: [ALARM]: monit:memory_usage memory usage increased by 10.5%, exceeds increase threshold 10% (previous: 48.4%, current: 58.9%)**
...
...
**INFO     root:__init__.py:93 -------------------- fixture setup_env teardown starts --------------------**
**INFO     tests.generic_config_updater.test_monitor_config:test_monitor_config.py:104 Rolled back to original checkpoint**
INFO     tests.common.gu_utils:gu_utils.py:335 Commands: config rollback test
DEBUG    tests.common.devices.base:base.py:129 /root/mars/workspace/sonic-**mgmt/tests/common/devices/base.py::_run_wrapper#115: [r-2700-42] AnsibleModule::shell, args=["config rollback test"], kwargs={"module_ignore_errors": true}**
...
INFO     tests.common.gu_utils:gu_utils.py:265 Commands: config list-checkpoints
...
INFO     root:__init__.py:102 -------------------- fixture setup_env teardown ends --------------------
**ERROR    tests.common.plugins.memory_utilization:__init__.py:155 Memory errors detected in fixture teardown: [ALARM]: monit:memory_usage memory usage increased by 10.5%, exceeds increase threshold 10% (previous: 48.4%, current: 58.9%)**

The memory checker failed:
Failed: [ALARM]: monit:memory_usage memory usage increased by 10.5%, exceeds increase threshold 10% (previous: 48.4%, current: 58.9%)
This monit memory usage is the total memory usage in the system.
In the techsupport dump collected right after the test failure, the memory usage had already dropped to under the test threshold:
```
               total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available
Mem:         8027772     4052608      777124      288372     3795720     3975164
Swap:              0           0           0
```
The used memory here is 4052608(~3.9G), which is ~51%(threadhold 58.4%)

And also there is another memory utilization issue: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/20377, the monit has a 1 mins interval to collet the memory usage(https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/files/image_config/monit/monitrc#L19), this makes the GCU test even more unstable as the configuration changes a lot during the test.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the test generic_config_updater/test_monitor_config.py on SN2700/SN2700-A1 platform with master branch.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The memory checker should collect the memory usage after all the configuration teardown. And should wait for the switch to go into a stable state.

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Output of `show version`

```shell

SONiC.master_RC_integration.4-c0c581a5c_Internal
```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

resolution.title: [cacl] Wait for BGP after dummy ACL cleanup reload
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:

Wait for BGP convergence after the `dummy_acl_rules` fixture reloads the original configuration. Without this stabilization, the next CACL test can record its memory-utilization baseline while the DUT is still recovering from `config_reload`, then report a false whole-system memory increase during teardown even though every test body passes.

The physical reproduction was:

```text
monit:memory_usage memory usage increased by 17.3%,
previous 19.6%, current 36.9%, threshold 10%
```

Fixes #24059

### Test result

Static validation on current master:

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `python3 -m py_compile tests/cacl/test_cacl_application.py`: passed.
- Targeted pre-commit: passed, including AST and flake8.

Physical 202605 validation:

- Image: tagged `SONiC.20260510.16`, build commit `623030c305`.
- Testbed / DUT: `testbed-bjw-can-720dt-2` / `bjw-can-720dt-2`, Arista-720DT-G48S4, `mx`.
- Checkout: fresh `internal-202605` with exact sonic-mgmt #27285 commits plus this one-line fix.
- Matching `deploy-mg`: passed; `test_pretest.py`: 11 passed, 3 skipped.
- Baseline full module: all five applicable test bodies passed, but the final teardown errored on the memory alarm above.
- Module-wide `--enable_monit_refresh`: 5 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0 in 30:26, but added substantial runtime.
- Refresh marker only on `test_caclmgrd_syslog`: 5 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0 in 24:28.
- This reload-stabilization fix, normal memory checking, no refresh marker:
  - run 1: 5 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0 in 22:27;
  - run 2: 5 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0 in 22:30.

The stabilization matches the existing `clean_scale_rules` precedent and avoids disabling memory checking, raising thresholds, or paying the Monit retry cost.

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

`test_cacl_acl_loader` uses `dummy_acl_rules`. Its teardown calls `config_reload`, and the next case is `test_caclmgrd_syslog`. The memory fixture starts the next baseline before the post-reload system has necessarily reconverged.

The repository already solves the analogous boundary in `clean_scale_rules` by passing `wait_for_bgp=True`. This PR applies the same stabilization to `dummy_acl_rules`.

#### How did you do it?

Added `wait_for_bgp=True` to the existing safe `config_reload` in `dummy_acl_rules` teardown. No memory thresholds, platform exceptions, or plugin behavior changed.

#### How did you verify/test it?

See Test result. Two consecutive physical full-module runs passed with memory checking enabled and effectively no runtime increase versus the failing baseline.

#### Any platform specific information?

Reproduced on Arista-720DT-G48S4 / MX, but the fixture ordering issue is platform-independent.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A.

### Documentation

N/A.

### Repeated tagged-image validation

After the initial two successful full-module runs, the same one-line fix was run **10 additional times sequentially** on the same physical tagged-image setup with normal memory checking and no Monit refresh marker.

| Run | Result | Pytest runtime | Memory alarms |
|---|---|---:|---:|

| 2 | 5 passed, 4 skipped | 1343.54s | 0 |

| 9 | 5 passed, 4 skipped | 1337.91s | 0 |
| 10 | 5 passed, 4 skipped | 1337.46s | 0 |

Aggregate: **10/10 runs passed**, **50 applicable test executions passed**, **40 topology skips**, **zero errors**, **zero memory alarms**. Mean runtime 1347.09s (22:27), min 1337.46s, max 1363.46s, sample SD 9.89s. Including the two earlier stabilization runs, the fix has passed **12 consecutive full-module runs** on tagged `SONiC.20260510.16`.
